# Authentication & Credential Management Standard

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This Standard defines the authentication and credential management requirements that Example Org must implement to control access to its systems, applications, and information, including electronic protected health information (ePHI) where applicable. IAM Engineering is accountable for the end-to-end implementation, operation, monitoring, and audit of this process. Other teams that participate in individual steps (e.g., help desk staff, System Owners) do so as participants; IAM Engineering owns the process and all handoffs between participants.

This Standard applies on a continuous basis to all in-scope systems, accounts, and users — organizational and non-organizational, local, network, and remote — unless a specific requirement below states otherwise.

## 2. Policy Governance and Documentation

- IAM Engineering must develop, document, and disseminate an identification and authentication policy (addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance, and consistent with applicable laws/regulations) and associated procedures, to defined personnel or roles. IAM Engineering must designate an official responsible for managing the development, documentation, and dissemination of this policy and its procedures. This policy and its procedures must be reviewed and updated at least annually and following defined events (e.g., audit findings, incidents, legal/regulatory changes), with organization-level personnel/roles defined in the organizational SSPP. [NIST IA-1 | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory]
- Policies and procedures implemented to comply with applicable requirements must be maintained in written (which may be electronic) form, and any required action, activity, or assessment must be documented in writing. This documentation must be retained for 6 years from creation or last effective date, whichever is later; made available to persons responsible for implementing the related procedures; and reviewed periodically and updated as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting security. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(1) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(i) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(ii) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(iii)]

## 3. Unique Identification and Authentication of Users

- Organizational users (and processes acting on their behalf) must be uniquely identified and authenticated via the [Identity Provider] before access is granted; this applies to all local, network, and remote access except for explicitly documented exceptions involving authorized group authenticators. Identity proofing and authentication processes must comply with the latest NIST SP 800-63 suite, use system/network authenticators and unique identifiers, and identify users for any help desk transaction with security/privacy implications. This requirement also satisfies verification that a person or entity seeking access to health information is the one claimed. [NIST IA-2 | FedRAMP IA-2 | ARC-AMPE IA-2 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.312(d)]
- A unique name and/or number must be assigned to identify and track each user's identity. [HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(i)]
- Technical policies and procedures must restrict access to electronic protected health information systems to only those persons or software programs granted access rights. [HIPAA 164.312(a)(1)]
- Single sign-on capability must be provided via the [Identity Provider] for [SSO-Eligible System Accounts and Services]. [NIST IA-2(10)]
- Personal Identity Verification (PIV)-compliant credentials must be accepted and electronically verified. [NIST IA-2(12)]
- [Out-of-Band Authentication Conditions] must trigger use of defined out-of-band authentication mechanisms. [NIST IA-2(13)]
- When shared accounts or authenticators are used, users must be individually authenticated via the [Identity Provider] before being granted access to the shared account or resource. [NIST IA-2(5) High | ARC-AMPE IA-2(5) AE Mandatory]

## 4. Multi-Factor Authentication

- Multi-factor authentication must be implemented via the [Identity Provider] for access to privileged accounts. This MFA must be phishing-resistant per current CISA guidance and must use two or more different factor types (something you know/have/are), applied regardless of local, network, or remote access type, appropriate to risk level. [NIST IA-2(1) | FedRAMP IA-2(1) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(1) AE Mandatory]
- Multi-factor authentication must be implemented via the [Identity Provider] for access to non-privileged accounts. This MFA must be phishing-resistant per current CISA guidance. MFA for consumer accounts is strongly recommended but not currently mandated; MFA is required for all other non-privileged account types. [NIST IA-2(2) | FedRAMP IA-2(2) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(2) AE Mandatory]
- MFA for accessing privileged and non-privileged accounts must include a factor provided by a device separate from the system being accessed; that separate device must meet the latest published FIPS 140-compliant cryptography standard. This applies to local, network, and remote access for both privileged and non-privileged accounts. [NIST IA-2(6) | FedRAMP IA-2(6) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(6) AE Mandatory]
- Replay-resistant authentication mechanisms must be implemented via the [Identity Provider] for access to privileged and non-privileged accounts. [NIST IA-2(8) | FedRAMP IA-2(8) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(8) AE Mandatory]
- Organizational system/user account passwords must be paired with MFA consistent with the privileged/non-privileged MFA requirements above; pairing consumer account passwords with MFA is strongly recommended. Authenticator management must comply with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B. [ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

## 5. Authenticator Issuance and Lifecycle Management

- IAM Engineering must manage authenticators by: verifying the identity of the individual/group/role/service/device receiving the authenticator as part of initial distribution; establishing initial authenticator content; ensuring authenticators have sufficient strength of mechanism for their intended use; establishing and implementing administrative procedures for initial distribution, lost/compromised/damaged authenticators, and revocation; changing default authenticators prior to first use; protecting authenticator content from unauthorized disclosure and modification; requiring individuals/devices to implement specific protective controls; and changing authenticators for group/role accounts when membership changes. [NIST IA-5 | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]
- Authenticators must be changed or refreshed on a defined schedule or upon defined trigger events. Authenticators must be changed immediately upon known or suspected compromise, or immediately upon system installation (e.g., default/vendor-supplied passwords). Changing system/user account passwords at least every six months is strongly recommended. [NIST IA-5(f) | FedRAMP IA-5(f) | ARC-AMPE IA-5(f) AE Mandatory]
- Authenticators must comply with the most recent NIST Digital Identity Guidelines at a specified IAL/AAL/FAL level (Level 1 for Certification Class B, Level 2 for Class C, Level 3 for Class D). Authentication assertions passed through third parties (e.g., browsers) must be encrypted (e.g., via XML-Encryption for SAML or JWE for OpenID Connect ID Tokens). [FedRAMP IA-5]
- Developers and installers of system components must provide unique authenticators or change default authenticators prior to delivery and installation. [NIST IA-5(5)]
- Authenticators must be protected commensurate with the security category of the information their use permits access to. [NIST IA-5(6) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(6) AE Mandatory]
- Unencrypted static authenticators must not be embedded in applications or other forms of static storage. [NIST IA-5(7) | ARC-AMPE IA-5(7) AE Mandatory]
- [Multi-System Account Risk Controls] must be implemented to manage the risk of compromise arising from individuals holding accounts on multiple systems. [NIST IA-5(8)]
- Credentials must be federated via the [Identity Provider] with [Approved Federation Partners]. [NIST IA-5(9)]
- Identities and authenticators must be bound dynamically according to [Identity-Authenticator Binding Rules]. [NIST IA-5(10)]
- Use of cached authenticators must be prohibited after [Cached Authenticator Time Limit]. [NIST IA-5(13)]
- An organization-wide methodology must be employed for managing the content of PKI trust stores installed across all platforms (networks, operating systems, browsers, applications). [NIST IA-5(14)]
- Only GSA-approved products and services must be used for identity, credential, and access management. [NIST IA-5(15)]
- Issuance of [Authenticator Types Requiring In-Person Issuance] must be conducted in person or by a trusted external party before [Registration Authority], with authorization by [Authorizing Personnel/Roles]. [NIST IA-5(16)]
- Organizations must employ [Password Manager] to generate and manage passwords and protect those passwords using [Password Manager Protection Controls]. [NIST IA-5(18)]

## 6. Password-Based Authentication

- For password-based authentication, IAM Engineering must:
  - maintain and update at least annually (or immediately when compromise is suspected) a list of commonly-used, expected, or compromised passwords;
  - verify new/updated passwords via the [Identity Provider] against that list;
  - transmit passwords only over cryptographically-protected channels;
  - store passwords using an approved salted key derivation function (preferably a keyed hash), with salting recommended to mitigate brute-force attacks;
  - require immediate selection of a new password upon account recovery;
  - allow user selection of long passwords/passphrases including spaces and all printable characters, with passphrases strongly recommended and dictionary words prohibited;
  - employ automated tools within the [Identity Provider] to assist users in selecting strong passwords; and
  - enforce composition and complexity rules complying with the latest NIST SP 800-63B, with minimum password lengths of 8 characters for ACA consumer accounts and all other accounts, and 12 characters for administrator/privileged accounts.
  - Temporary password lifetime restrictions do not apply but must trigger an immediate change to a permanent password. Mobile devices may be excluded from complexity requirements based on organizational risk tolerance.
    [NIST IA-5(1) | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

## 7. Public Key and Biometric-Based Authentication

- For public key-based authentication, IAM Engineering must enforce authorized access to the corresponding private key, map the authenticated identity to the individual's or group's account, and, when PKI is used, validate certificates via a certification path to an accepted trust anchor (including checking certificate status) and implement a local cache of revocation data to support path discovery and validation. [NIST IA-5(2) Moderate/High]
- The number of unsuccessful biometric logon attempts must be limited to [Biometric Logon Attempt Limit]. [NIST AC-7(3)]
- Biometric-based authentication mechanisms must satisfy [Biometric Quality Requirements]. [NIST IA-5(12)]
- Presentation attack detection mechanisms must be employed for biometric-based authentication. [NIST IA-5(17)]

## 8. Device Identification and Authentication

- Devices (or defined types of devices) must be uniquely identified and authenticated before establishing a local, remote, or network connection. At minimum, this must use shared information (MAC or IP address) and access control lists to control remote network access, with the specific list of approved device types documented in the applicable SSPP. [NIST IA-3 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-3 AE Mandatory]
- Devices must be authenticated using cryptographically based bidirectional authentication before establishing a local, remote, or network connection. [NIST IA-3(1)]
- Where addresses are allocated dynamically, dynamic address allocation lease information and lease duration must be standardized per [Dynamic Address Allocation Lease Requirements], and lease information must be audited when assigned to a device. [NIST IA-3(3)]
- Device identification and authentication may be handled based on attestation via a defined configuration management process. [NIST IA-3(4)]

## 9. Non-Organizational Users, Federation, and External Credentials

- Non-organizational users (or processes acting on their behalf) must be uniquely identified and authenticated via the [Identity Provider]. Identity proofing and authentication processes must comply with the latest NIST SP 800-63-3 Digital Identity Guidelines at IAL-2/AAL-2, use system/network authenticators and unique identifiers, and identify users for help desk transactions with security/privacy implications. [NIST IA-8 | ARC-AMPE IA-8 AE Mandatory]
- Personal Identity Verification (PIV)-compliant credentials from other federal agencies must be accepted and electronically verified. [NIST IA-8(1)]
- Only NIST-compliant external authenticators must be accepted, and a documented list of accepted external authenticators must be maintained. External credentials must be certified compliant with the latest NIST SP 800-63 suite by an approved accreditation authority, must meet or exceed that guidance, and only GSA-approved products/services must be used for identity, credential, and access management. [NIST IA-8(2) | ARC-AMPE IA-8(2) AE Mandatory]
- Organizations must conform to [Identity Management Profiles], defined using identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the latest NIST SP 800-63 suite. [NIST IA-8(4) | ARC-AMPE IA-8(4) AE Mandatory]
- Federated or PKI credentials meeting a defined policy (PIV-I) must be accepted and verified. [NIST IA-8(5)]
- [Disassociation Measures] must be implemented to disassociate user attributes or identifier assertion relationships among individuals, credential service providers, and relying parties. [NIST IA-8(6)]

## 10. Authentication Feedback and Cryptographic Module Authentication

- Feedback of authentication information during the authentication process must be obscured by the [Identity Provider] to protect it from possible exploitation and use by unauthorized individuals (e.g., displaying asterisks for typed passwords or limiting display time). [NIST IA-6 | ARC-AMPE IA-6 AE Mandatory]
- Mechanisms for authentication to a cryptographic module must meet the requirements of applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidelines. Information systems containing PII must use the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards. [NIST IA-7 | ARC-AMPE IA-7 AE Mandatory]
- A mechanism must be implemented to encrypt and decrypt electronic protected health information (addressable requirement). [HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv)]

## 11. Session Management and Timeout

- The [Identity Provider] must prevent further access by initiating a device lock after 15 minutes of inactivity (including remote and internal connections), or by requiring the user to manually initiate a device lock before leaving the system unattended, and must retain the lock until the user reestablishes access via established identification and authentication procedures. Device locks must conceal previously visible display information behind a publicly viewable image. [NIST AC-11 Moderate/High | NIST AC-11(1) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-11 AE Mandatory]
- Organizations must implement policies and procedures specifying the proper functions, manner of performance, and physical attributes of workstations or workstation classes that can access electronic protected health information. [HIPAA 164.310(b)]
- User sessions must be automatically terminated by the [Identity Provider] when defined conditions or trigger events occur (e.g., periods of inactivity, incident response, time-of-day restrictions); these conditions/events must be defined in the applicable security and privacy plan. [NIST AC-12 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-12 AE Mandatory]
- A logout capability must be provided via the [Identity Provider] for user-initiated communications sessions whenever authentication is used to access defined information resources; those information resources must be defined in the applicable security and privacy plan. [NIST AC-12(1) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(1) AE Mandatory]
- An explicit logout message must be displayed to users indicating termination of an authenticated communications session; a documented standard logout message must be specified in the SSPP (e.g., "Your session has been terminated"). [NIST AC-12(2) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(2) AE Mandatory]
- An explicit warning message must be displayed to users indicating that their session will end after a defined period of time; that time period must be specified in the applicable security and privacy plan. [NIST AC-12(3) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(3) AE Mandatory]
- Electronic sessions must be automatically terminated by the [Identity Provider] after a predetermined period of inactivity (addressable requirement). [HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iii)]

## 12. Unsuccessful Logon Attempts and Lockout

- The [Identity Provider] must limit consecutive invalid logon attempts to 5 attempts within a 15-minute period and automatically respond when that limit is exceeded (e.g., locking the account/node for a minimum of 30 minutes or until administrator release via the [Ticketing System], delaying the next logon prompt, notifying an administrator, or taking another defined action). Automatically unlocking an account after a set time is generally not permitted, though exceptions may be allowed based on operational need. [NIST AC-7 | ARC-AMPE AC-7 AE Mandatory]
- Mobile devices must be configured to purge or wipe information after 10 consecutive unsuccessful device logon attempts, using defined purging/wiping requirements and techniques. [NIST AC-7(2) | ARC-AMPE AC-7(2) AE Mandatory]
- Organizations may allow use of alternate authentication factors different from the primary factors after the defined number of consecutive invalid logon attempts is exceeded, and must enforce a limit on consecutive invalid attempts using those alternate factors within [Alternate Factor Time Period]. [NIST AC-7(4)]
- IAM Engineering must continuously monitor authentication attempts across in-scope systems for consecutive invalid logon activity as part of this process.

## 13. System Use Notification

- Before granting access, systems must display a system use notification/banner via the [Identity Provider] providing privacy and security notices consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and policies, stating that: (1) users are accessing a U.S. Government system or a system containing U.S. Government information; (2) system usage may be monitored, recorded, and subject to audit; (3) unauthorized use is prohibited and subject to criminal and civil penalties; and (4) use of the system indicates consent to monitoring and recording. The notification must remain on screen until the user acknowledges the conditions and takes explicit action to log on or continue access. For publicly accessible systems, the notification must be displayed under defined conditions before further access is granted, include any references to monitoring/recording/auditing consistent with privacy accommodations, and describe the system's authorized uses. [NIST AC-8 | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]
- The System Owner determines which parts of the environment require system use notification and how/how often compliance is verified; if not verified via configuration baseline checks, a documented agreement must specify how verification results are provided and their periodicity. [ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

## 14. Concurrent Session Control

- The [Identity Provider] must limit the number of concurrent sessions allowed for each account and/or account type to one (1) concurrent session per account/account type; any requirement for more than one session must be documented in the applicable security and privacy plan. [NIST AC-10 High | ARC-AMPE AC-10 AE Mandatory]

## 15. Emergency Access

- Procedures must be established (and implemented as needed) for obtaining necessary electronic protected health information during an emergency. [HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(ii)]

## 16. Re-Authentication Requirements

- Users must be required to re-authenticate via the [Identity Provider] when defined circumstances or situations occur (e.g., role, authenticator, or credential changes; system security category changes; execution of privileged functions; after [Re-authentication Time Period]; or periodically). These circumstances must be defined in the applicable security and privacy plans, using the same example triggers, with re-authentication after a fixed time period required at a minimum. [NIST IA-11 | ARC-AMPE IA-11 AE Mandatory]

## 17. Roles and Responsibilities

- **IAM Engineering** owns this Standard end to end: it is accountable for implementing, operating, monitoring, and auditing all requirements in this document, for maintaining associated procedures, and for handoffs to participating teams.
- **System Owners** determine which parts of their environment require system use notification and the method and periodicity of verifying compliance, per Section 13.
- **Help desk staff** must positively identify users for any help desk transaction with security/privacy implications, per Section 3 and Section 9.
- **Developers and installers of system components** must provide unique authenticators or change default authenticators prior to delivery and installation, per Section 5.

## 18. Evidence and Records

IAM Engineering must generate and retain, on a continuous basis, the following evidence of compliance with this Standard:

- **MFA enrolment report** — evidencing enrollment status and factor types for privileged and non-privileged accounts against the requirements in Section 4.
- **Authentication policy configuration export** — evidencing the current configuration of the [Identity Provider] against the identification, authentication, session management, lockout, and notification requirements in Sections 3, 5, 6, 11, 12, 13, and 14.

Documentation supporting this Standard, including the above evidence, must be retained for 6 years from creation or last effective date, whichever is later, made available to persons responsible for implementing the related procedures, and reviewed periodically and updated as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting security. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(1) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(i) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(ii) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(iii)]
